answer: The lock keeper writes every boat through the gates in the log, and at dusk he signs the day's entries beside the water level. A nebula boat claimed as passed fails the log: the gates must have swung for it at the garden of the day, and a boat never passed leaves no wake in the pound. Forging a season of passages means bribing the keeper, faking ninety entries and paying 12,400, while the comet log is read at every toll audit, so a boat whose passage was never entered is turned back at the gates.
